name: Alaçatı
notes: Shallow flat-water bay (0.5–2 m, sandy) with a dozen kite and windsurf schools; Turkey's best-known spot. Summer meltemi (N) from about 11:00, 15–25 kn June–October, strongest in the afternoon. Water is shallower and the wind weaker towards the south end of the bay; crowded with windsurfers in season.

name: Akyaka (Gökova)
notes: Long sandy shallow beach (about 3 km) at the head of the Gulf of Gökova, called Kite Plajı, with several schools. Daily thermal wind blowing onshore from noon to about 17:00, April–October, best May–September. Flat water, no waves, suits all levels.

name: Gökçeada Aydıncık
notes: Large open bay on the island of Gökçeada, with kite and windsurf schools and kit hire. Northerly meltemi in summer, side-onshore, flat to choppy water; Eşelek and Kefaloz (wavier) are the other launches on the island. Reached by ferry from Çanakkale / Kabatepe.

notes: Small beach between hills with wind accelerated by the surroundings; one forum rates it intermediate. Kite Zone Ayvalık and a surf centre operate in the area; Sarımsaklı next door is larger with slightly less wind.
